research_question: Under an identical regularised Logistic Regression framework, how does retrospective walk-forward classification performance differ across four pre-specified standalone feature families—EMA-aware technical, cross-market, macroeconomic, and broad sentiment/risk proxies—when predicting Tesla's five-session forward-versus-trailing mean-close direction?

macro_source_snapshots.change_construction: Compute release-to-release changes at monthly source frequency before backward as-of merging to TSLA trading dates; preserve true zero changes.

target.name: Rolling five-trading-day mean-price trend
target.interpretation_boundary: classification target, not trading win rate or next-week endpoint return

moving_average_state_definitions.role: persistent trend state, not a one-day crossover event

uncertainty.family_comparison_multiplicity: Holm adjustment across the three Technical-versus-alternative contrasts, separately for development OOF and retrospective audit

overlap_robustness.method: five phase-specific refits using Eligible_Row_ID modulo 5
overlap_robustness.anchor: Eligible_Row_ID 0 is the first target-eligible row on or after 2016-10-03
overlap_robustness.purpose: use non-overlapping future five-day windows within each phase in both development and audit
overlap_robustness.caveat: successive labels within a phase still share a comparison window, so phase results are robustness checks rather than independent trials

rq_boundaries.rq2: feature-family comparison under common Logistic Regression
rq_boundaries.rq3: model-family comparison is out of scope for this package
rq_boundaries.rq4: economic backtesting is out of scope for this package

claim_boundary: All results use previously inspected 2016-2026 history and are retrospective. They cannot be described as prospectively untouched confirmation.
